rationale: The O'Kelly et al. source explicitly states that their simulation framework uses adaptive importance-sampling methods to "estimate the probability of an accident under a base distribution governing standard traffic behavior" (S-EVID-003-R1). It further details the goal to "evaluate the probability of a dangerous event pγ := P0 (f (X) ≤ γ) for some threshold γ" using a "base distribution P0 that models standard traffic behavior and X ∼ P0 be a realization of the simulation" (S-EVID-003-R2). This directly supports the claim that rare-event simulation can estimate a risk metric conditional on a modeled traffic distribution, simulator, and safety threshold. The introduction also contrasts this approach with the need for "billions of miles in order to statistically validate performance claims" from real-world testing, supporting the 'rather than proving unconditional safety from total test miles' aspect. The claim's scope, 'O'Kelly et al. highway research case study using importance sampling; not a regulatory method,' is consistent with the source's description as a research preprint and its stated limitations regarding regulatory approval and conditional nature.
evidence_locators: PDF p. 2, base distribution and simulation inputs
